thread:
incident-bot: [P1] High generation latency and increased error rate observed in eu-central-1 for streaming endpoints. Paging oncall.

maria (oncall): I see p95 jump ~3x and a tail of stream disconnects. Routing metrics show a batch of traffic hitting a legacy model variant. Marking priority P1 and invoking mitigation runbook.

lee (sre): joining. Quick check: `curl -s https://internal-metrics/routing?region=eu-central-1 | jq .`
lee (sre): routing table shows a recent policy flip sending ~18% of traffic to model-legacy-v1, which has slower token generation. Correlating with deploy window ~10m ago.

zoe (ops): if traffic is misrouted we'll overload slower instances. I can add burst nodes and pin critical routes to fastgen pool. Applying temporary route override and spinning up 6 extra fastgen replicas.

avi (comms): drafting statuspage message. Keeping it customer-friendly and non-technical. Posting draft below for quick review.

avi (comms): STATUSPAGE DRAFT:
```
Summary: We are investigating generation latency and intermittent streaming failures affecting some customers in eu-central-1.
Impact: A subset of streaming and generation requests may be slower than normal or disconnect. Not all customers are affected; fallbacks are in place.
Current status: Engineering has applied temporary routing overrides and additional capacity. We are monitoring performance.
Guidance: If you experience degraded responses, please retry. Account teams will reach out to impacted customers.
Next update: We plan to provide an update within 20 minutes.
```

kate (legal): small wording change: replace "We plan to provide an update within 20 minutes" with "We aim to provide an update within approximately 20 minutes." avoid exact promises. Also prefer "may be slower or disconnect" -> "may be slower or experience interruptions".

avi (comms): updated wording per legal.

maria (oncall): technical owner note: root cause suspected misapplied routing rule during a config rollout. Keep public line high-level as written.

lee (sre): publishing internal remediation snippet to #eng-oncall: `./tools/routing-ctl override --region eu-central-1 --route fastgen; kubectl scale deploy/fastgen -n prod --replicas=14`

zoe (ops): capacity scale started. routing override applied. Observability: early signs of p95 improving. I'll hold on rollback instructions until stable.

maria (oncall): go ahead and publish statuspage. Tag sales-desk for account notifications and drop a short internal TL;DR in #eng-oncall.

avi (comms): Published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/eu-central-gen-3076543210

incident-bot: [STATUSPAGE POSTED] eu-central-gen-3076543210 posted by avi.

sales-desk: received. building list of affected accounts from traffic logs and will DM them with the templated note.

-- 25 minutes later --

lee (sre): p95 back down to near baseline, stream disconnects dropping. Routing override holding; legacy variant traffic reduced to <1%.

zoe (ops): autoscaler stabilized, removing burst nodes in a controlled rollback.

avi (comms): drafting resolved notice for statuspage.

avi (comms): RESOLVED DRAFT:
```
Summary: The generation latency and streaming interruption affecting eu-central-1 has been resolved.
Impact: Some customers experienced slower responses and intermittent stream interruptions during the incident window.
Resolution: A routing rollback and temporary capacity adjustments reduced load on slower model variants and restored normal performance.
Follow-up: We will produce a post-incident report with corrective actions and a timeline. If you still see issues, contact support.
```

kate (legal): approved.

maria (oncall): approved. Please publish resolved and close incident. Open a follow-up ticket to review config rollout safety checks.

avi (comms): Resolved notice published to statuspage and sent to affected accounts via sales-desk. Closing incident.

incident-bot: [RESOLVED] eu-central-gen-3076543210 resolved. Total duration ~37m.

maria (oncall): filing follow-up: ENG-INC-2026: add gating to routing config rollouts and expand canary checks. Thanks everyone for the quick response. :tada:
